title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 100
paragraphs: When Xerxes had had the army numbered and arranged in its divisions, he resolved to drive through it himself and review it, and he then proceeded to do so. Driving past each nation in turn in a chariot, he inquired about them, and his scribes wrote down the names, until he had gone from end to end both of the cavalry and of the infantry. When he had done this, the ships were drawn down into the sea, and Xerxes, changing from his chariot to a Sidonian ship, sat down under a golden canopy and sailed along past the prows, questioning each contingent as he had done with the land army and having the answers written down. The captains had taken their ships out to about four plethra from the beach and were holding them there, all with the prows turned in an even line toward the shore and the fighting men fully armed for war; Xerxes inspected them sailing in the channel between the prows and the beach.
